label: copy-phase input e, early, when k/y/e come next
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is e (99% of mass). It never fires on e in the original phase or at the delimiter. It is concentrated at early recall positions (recall_idx 1-3, about 99% of mass), with the strongest activations when e is the first original token being fed back right after <DEL>. Within copy-phase e inputs it fires sparsely (about 7%). It is much more likely when the token being output now is k, y or e, or when y is output next. Top examples look like ...e k y... / e y... sequences. Many digits in the sequence suppress it. Being an e input in the copy phase is close to necessary (98% recall) but far from sufficient. The output-token conditions get precision only to about 0.6, so the remaining selectivity is not fully captured.
